hook_text: A truck of free food arrives every week. Sounds like kindness. Watch what happens to the town's own farmers.
clip_script: The old proverb holds the entire topic: give a man a fish and he eats today; teach him to fish and he eats for life. Aid arrives in exactly those flavours. The FISH is humanitarian aid — the food parcel, the rescue boat, the blankets when the river takes the street. When the KwaZulu-Natal floods came, nobody standing on a roof needed a fishing lesson; they needed water, shelter and medicine, at speed. Judge the fish on speed and reach and it is magnificent. But see its built-in ceiling: the fish feeds today. It cannot lay the drainage that would have kept the street dry in the first place. The FISHING LESSON is technical aid — the engineer who trains the town's water technicians, the specialists who teach rural nurses. The money is spent once; the skill keeps working for thirty years. That is why the lesson usually beats the fish — EXCEPT in mid-flood, when a lesson is useless and a boat is everything. Timing decides which aid is the right aid. And the quiet danger at the end: if the free fish keeps arriving every week, forever, the town's own fishermen cannot compete with free. They beach their boats. The town that once fed itself now waits for the truck — and that is DEPENDENCY: help meant as a bridge, hardening into a crutch.
visual_style: A single fish handed over morphing into a fishing rod being taught; flood water rising around a street as rescue boats arrive; a line of fishing boats slowly tipping onto a beach as a delivery truck's shadow grows; a bridge morphing into a crutch for the final beat.
mood: Warm then unsettling, closing thoughtful rather than bleak.
pacing: Gentle proverb open, urgent flood middle, slow-motion beat on the beached boats, crisp one-word landing on dependency.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and learn to weigh aid with evidence on both pans.
